key_insight: A benchmarked universal machine-learning potential enables scalable molecular dynamics to capture the temperature-driven charge-density-wave transition in monolayer 1T-TaS2 from Star-of-David order to the primitive hexagonal phase.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical finite-temperature simulation workflow for complex correlated materials where direct first-principles molecular dynamics is too costly.
method: DFT was used to benchmark universal ML interatomic potentials against displacement energies.
The UMA-s-1p1 potential was selected for large-scale MD simulations across heating and cooling cycles.
Temperature-dependent effective potential phonon calculations were combined with MD to track structural and vibrational CDW signatures.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that MD reproduced the experimentally observed phase sequence and that the selected potential achieved sufficient accuracy in DFT displacement-energy benchmarks.
watch_item: The results depend on careful potential benchmarking and may not transfer reliably to other CDW materials or unseen distortions without revalidation.
paper_title: Charge-Density-Wave Phase Transitions in Monolayer 1T-TaS2 from Universal Machine Learning Molecular Dynamics
